newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian government threatens striking workers.
newsitem.headline: Colombian government threatens striking workers.

text.p: The Colombian government threatened on Wednesday to cancel a wage accord with public sector workers after they staged a one-day strike in support of striking health workers.

A government statement called the one-day strike politically motivated, "unjust and rash." It said it had prompted President Ernesto Samper to order his economic team to "review all commitments made as part of the state labour agreement."
The government agreed to steep wage hikes as part of a deal ending a week-long strike by Colombia's estimated 800,000 public sector workers in February.
But presidential spokesman Carlos Castillo said that agreement had been violated by Wednesday's strike, so the wage deal was no longer binding.
Wilson Borja, head of the state workers' union known as Fenaltrase, said the government had failed to respect most terms of the February pact.

Labour leaders noted that the strike by about 120,000 workers in the state-run health sector, which began on Tuesday of last week, was called because the government had failed to make good on a previous pledge to raise wages for doctors, nurses and other health workers significantly.
Wednesday's strike was barely noticeable in the capital, where shops and banks opened for business as usual and there were no reports that public transportation had been affected.
Authorities said there were no incidents of strike-related violence.

Hernando Hernandez, head of the state oil workers union, said all of its members had downed tools for 24 hours beginning at 6 a.m. (1100 GMT). But spokesmen for the state oil company Ecopetrol said production was not affected.
